maya: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selection change I see a consistent tail-latency spike on short-prefix requests. KV cache hit rate drops ~18% for seq len <= 64.
liam: ugh. which commit? any nsys captures?
maya: commit 4f2b9a8, the 'prefer-vec16' path. I captured an nsys trace on staging (20k reqs, replayed). attaching notes.
maya: ```
nsys profile --output=kv-prefetch-1918765432 --trace=cuda,osrt -t cuda,osrt ./run_inference --replay workloads/staging_short_prefix.json
# export: run -> /artifacts/kv-prefetch-1918765432.nsys-rep
```
maya: Quick observations from the timeline: dispatch thread waits ~6-9ms more per request, then we see a memcpy burst right before kernel launch. KV hit callbacks appear delayed.
sam: pdfetto/trace would help for cross-thread timing. but first: did kernel-selection now choose a fallback kernel for seq<=32? that could force an extra staging memcpy for quantized weights.
liam: good point. I grep'd the model profile and the selector now prefers 'matmul_mixed' for small batches. that kernel has a pre-launch pack step.
tess: can you dump the kernel timeline snippet? even a short list is fine.
maya: pasted snippet from nsys timeline (condensed):
```
[dispatch] enqueue request 0x7f.. -> wait 1.2ms
memcpy H2D 2.4ms
kernel matmul_mixed grid(64) block(256) 0.6ms
kv_lookup callback 0.1ms -> hit:false
memcpy D2H 1.8ms
```
liam: that memcpy H2D looks suspicious — KV cache should avoid H2D on hits. are hits being demoted? maybe prefix hashing changed.
sam: run a targeted perfetto with perfetto-probes for thread wakeups + nvtx markers. command: 
```
perfetto -c perfetto_config.pbtxt -o /tmp/trace.perfetto && python3 tools/trace_viewer.py /tmp/trace.perfetto
```
perf-bot: nsys report uploaded: https://storage.internal/runs/1918765432/kv-prefetch-1918765432.nsys-rep :file_folder: 
liam: noted. maya can you also capture env with FORCE_KERNEL=vec8 and FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_mixed to compare? if vec8 avoids the pack memcpy we should see hit rate recover.
maya: running both now on staging; I'll replay the same seed and drop links when done. ETA ~18m.
tess: also add the KV metrics: kv.hits, kv.misses, kv.latency_histogram for the run. we need per-prefix length breakdown.
maya: copying sample logs for one run:
```
KV_STATS prefix_len=16 hits=4123 misses=512 hit_rate=88.9%
KV_STATS prefix_len=32 hits=9812 misses=2032 hit_rate=82.8%
KV_STATS prefix_len=64 hits=1502 misses=298 hit_rate=83.5%
TAIL_LAT p99=54ms p95=28ms baseline_p99=36ms
```
liam: ok that's consistent with an additional memcpy path on the chosen kernel. hypothesis: selector added 'generic_pack' fallback for mixed-quantized kernels which triggers D2H/H2D during prefix checks.
sam: we should also check whether prefix cache keys changed serialization after the kernel change (endian/packing). small chance cache lookup returns miss due to format mismatch.
maya: good call — diffing serialization shows an additional header byte for 'kernel_id' in the new selector. looks like we accidentally include kernel_id in the cache key for vec16 path.
liam: that's the bug then. kernel_id shouldn't be part of the cache key. bandaid: strip kernel_id from cache key generation and re-run a small replay.
maya: applied patch locally, re-ran 2k replay: hit rates back up around +16% and tail p99 dropped ~12ms. pushing a PR now.
tess: please add a unit test that verifies cache key invariance across selector changes.
maya: will do. thanks all :tada:
liam: great catch. when PR lands let's schedule a quick canary on prod-dedicated for 1 hour and monitor kv.hit_rate and tail latency.
perf-bot: regression-check: linking CI perf run -> https://ci.internal/runs/1918765432/compare (baseline vs patched).
maya: tagging @oncall-runtime FYI for the canary.
liam: dropping a follow-up note in the rollout checklist with mitigation steps if hit rate drops again.
